name: Speech & occupational therapy (category guide)
summary: AHPC-registered speech and OT for expat kids and adults — private cash rates, EIPIC/PPIP citizenship gates, and why public early-intervention seats rarely open to EP children.
body: Speech-language therapists and occupational therapists practising in Singapore must be registered with the Allied Health Professions Council (AHPC) — ask for the name on the register before you buy a package. Public early-intervention programmes (EIPIC / PPIP-style seats) are built around citizen/PR children; EP/DP families usually land in private clinics at roughly S$150–250+ per hour, with assessments billed separately. Hospital outpatient therapy waits can be long even when referrals exist; private multidisciplinary centres trade cost for speed. Insurers often carve paediatric developmental therapy out of group medical or cap sessions tightly — get the schedule in writing. For school-age kids, align therapy goals with the receiving school’s learning-support process rather than collecting uncoordinated private reports. Adults post-stroke or workplace injury should pair AHPC therapy with WICA documentation when the injury is work-related. This is a category guide, not a ranked clinic league table.
